mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and higher corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns following a 0.5% increase in PAYEMS in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and can positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns when HOUST exceeds 1.7 million in more than 30% of cases, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests increased economic activity and supply, which can lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns when INDPRO exceeds 105 in more than 35% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real state and local government finance (RSAFS) indicates increased government spending, which can stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns when RSAFS growth exceeds 5% YoY in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which can lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% in more than 30% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and higher corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns when UNRATE is below 5% in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low, it indicates a favorable environment for economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: economic expansion with low interest rates
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2% and FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% in more than 35% of cases, this hypothesis fails.
